title: Coordination of Benefits Settings for Pharmacy Benefit Plan Designs
content:
When a member of the Pharmacy Benefit Plan may have other coverage, three design settings apply: how often a coordination-of-benefits questionnaire is sent, how long the member has to return it before claims pend for other-coverage review, and the method Northbridge Rx uses when it pays as the secondary payer.

| Plan design | Questionnaire sent every (months) | Days to return the questionnaire (calendar days) | Secondary-payer method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northbridge Rx HSA Saver | 12 | 45 | Standard coordination |
| Northbridge Rx Basic | 12 | 45 | Standard coordination |
| Northbridge Rx Value | 12 | 45 | Non-duplication |
| Northbridge Rx Select | 12 | 45 | Standard coordination |
| Northbridge Rx Plus | 12 | 45 | Standard coordination |
| Northbridge Rx Premier | 12 | 45 | Carve-out |

## Secondary-payer methods

| Method | How Northbridge Rx pays when it is secondary |
|---|---|
| Standard coordination | Pays up to its normal benefit. |
| Non-duplication | Pays only the excess of its benefit over the primary payment. |
| Carve-out | Reduces its benefit by the primary payment. |

## Illustration (hypothetical amounts)

Suppose, hypothetically, that the Northbridge Rx benefit on a claim would be 100.00 and the primary payer paid 70.00. Under non-duplication Northbridge Rx pays the excess of its benefit over the primary payment, 30.00. Under carve-out its benefit is reduced by the primary payment, also to 30.00 in this case. Under standard coordination it pays up to its normal benefit of 100.00.

The questionnaire cycle and the return period are the same on every design; only the secondary-payer method differs, with Northbridge Rx Value on non-duplication and Northbridge Rx Premier on carve-out.
